key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Linking spectral features to lattice instabilities can help interpret structural dynamics in halide-perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven or mixed instabilities.
Relate spectral features to mode symmetry, coupling and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compositions indicate that slow polar reorientations shift dielectric response to very low frequencies, while overdamped tilting produces persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative experimental validation or solar-cell performance testing, so device-level benefits remain unproven.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
